body.target_estimand: \(\tau_{\omega}(P)=\sum_{k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K}\omega_k E_Q[Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1]\) for any \(Q\in\mathcal M\) inducing \(P\)
body.estimand_functional: \(\tau_{\omega}(P)=\omega'\theta(P)=E_P[\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_kR_{k,c_0(k),P}(O)]\). On the observable equality model this also equals \(E_P[b(X)'R_P(O)]\) for every integrable feasible loading satisfying \(A'b(X)=\omega\); efficiency is determined separately by projecting the corresponding centered gradient onto \(\mathcal T_P\).

sampling_model.design: Observational staggered adoption in a balanced fixed-\(T\) panel under the literal global OVS period-by-period covariate-conditional DDD restrictions, using every cohort clean at each period.
sampling_model.units: \((O_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed panel units.
sampling_model.treatment: Enabling is absorbing through cohort \(G\), and effective treatment requires \(S=1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every cohort--eligibility cell entering a retained clean comparison has conditional probability at least \(\varepsilon\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For the proved attainment and efficiency-gap inference regimes, \(X\) has fixed finite support with masses bounded below.  Cell averages estimate every retained propensity, regression, shared-cell second cross-moment, and published normal moment.  The target estimator uses fixed-fold orthogonal OVS signals and \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), \(0<a<1/4\).  The gap estimator is the explicit rank-thresholded plug-in \(F_{z,\tau_n}(\widehat\mu)\), with absolute-eigenvalue thresholding for indefinite comparator KKT systems.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 4.1 establishes identification, Theorem 4.2 establishes asymptotic normality, and Remark 4.6 minimizes variance over constant componentwise clean-comparison weights.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: thm:observable-equivalence, thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient, thm:crossfit-attainment, prop:equality-frontier, and thm:finite-support-gap-wald

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.2 derives the covariate-specific optimal efficient influence function and efficiency bound for staggered DiD, while Theorem 4.1 establishes consistency, asymptotic normality, and attainment for the resulting estimator.

Theorem 2 identifies the panel DDD target, Theorem 3 identifies the repeated-cross-section target, Theorem 5 derives the panel efficient influence function, and Theorem 7 derives the repeated-cross-section efficient influence function.
Theorem 5.2 gives variance-minimizing conditional GMM instruments when the conditional covariance is singular and a consistent linear system exists.
Theorem 6.3 derives a fixed-weight stacked-DDD limit law and accounts for dependence from comparison units shared across stacks.
The paper derives an efficient imputation estimator under its event-study model and notes applications to triple-difference designs.
Theorem 3.1 establishes asymptotic linearity and Gaussian approximation for cross-fitted estimators based on orthogonal scores.

body.tldr: For the published global OVS staggered-DDD model, the exhaustive period-admissible normal vector \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) yields the canonical gradient \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\) and bound \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\); the clean-through-terminal local model and the aggregate pairwise-score family form two larger frontiers.  A fixed-support cross-fitted estimator attains the published bound.  Aggregate, localized, and published equality are diagnosed separately.  A bounded binary family makes all three normal closures coincide and gives the exact published-bound gain \(3/512\).  Away from equality and rank changes, an explicit finite-moment plug-in now gives pointwise Wald inference for the published-bound efficiency gap; the general-covariate growing-sieve result remains population-only.

project_justification.gap: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna establish identification, pairwise-score limit theory, and constant componentwise weighting, but do not exhaust the observed tangent space generated by every period-admissible clean cohort or derive inference for the resulting published-bound efficiency gap.
project_justification.niche: The published OVS model has more period-specific normal directions than either terminal clean-comparison contrasts or the localized clean-through-terminal model.  Singular comparison systems, shared outcome cells, and law-dependent comparator weights must all be differentiated coherently.
project_justification.fill: The note proves published observed-law tangent exhaustion, derives the singular Moore--Penrose canonical projection, constructs a fixed-support attaining estimator, and separates aggregate, localized, and published equality equations.  It also supplies a complete finite-moment map for the published-bound comparator gap, proves its selected-rank delta expansion and pointwise Wald validity away from boundaries, and certifies the bounded \(3/512\) regression-test family.

body.related_work: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna provide the identifying architecture, pairwise-score limit theory, and constant componentwise benchmark.  This note adds the exhaustive published OVS normal, its attaining fixed-support correction, and pointwise inference for the law-dependent comparator's published-bound gap.  Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie give related conditional efficiency results for staggered DiD, but not the eligibility-gap tangent system.  Newey informs generalized-inverse conditional-moment geometry; the affine quotient, absolute-eigenvalue selected-rank derivative, and DDD moment reconstruction are proved here.  Generic DML theory supplies the cross-fitting template but not the all-cohort shared-cell calculation.  The binary witness is a published-bound comparison because its OVS, localized, and aggregate normal closures are identical.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Population canonicality is pointwise at a conditional-mean interior law and permits singular or redundant normal coordinates.  Target attainment and gap inference are proved only for fixed finite covariate support.  The gap theorem assumes positive influence variance and is separated from equality by \(\delta_0>0\); it is not uniform across comparator or normal-rank changes.  The published-normal finite-sieve characterization does not establish a growing-sieve remainder for continuous covariates.
body.honest_scope: The note covers a fixed finite horizon and target set at interior laws admitting a full-data extension in the global OVS model.  It distinguishes the published bound \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), the localized bound \(V_{\mathrm{can}}\), and the aggregate score-family variance \(V_{\mathrm{agg}}\).  Cross-fitted target inference and plug-in efficiency-gap inference are pointwise fixed-support results.  The \(3/512\) witness is genuinely relative to the published bound because all three normal closures coincide.  No continuous-covariate gap Wald theorem, equality-boundary inference, or rank-uniform guarantee is claimed.
body.interpretation: There are three precision frontiers.  Conditional loading by \(b^\star(X)\) minimizes variance within the aggregate pairwise-score family.  Projection against \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) gives the larger localized model's bound.  Projection against the exhaustive \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) gives the smaller published bound.  A comparator reaches these frontiers when, respectively, \(N'\Gamma_P(X)b^{\mathrm{cmp}}=0\), \(E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P\mid X]=0\), and \(E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}\Psi_P\mid X]=0\).  The optional \(\texttt{triplediff}\) backend can report all three diagnostics and can expose gap Wald inference in the certified fixed-support branch.
